title: Compensation in Subtraction
objective: Compensation applies to subtraction too, but both numbers must adjust in the same direction to preserve the difference (unlike addition, where addends adjust in opposite directions).
studentQuestion: In subtraction, if I add 1 to this number, what do I need to do to the other one?
newIdea: The subtraction compensation rule — adjust both numbers the same way to keep the distance between them fixed — contrasted explicitly with addition's opposite-direction rule.

teaching.see: 19 is close to 20 — what if both numbers moved up together?
teaching.transform: 52 - 19 and 53 - 20 — same difference (33), because the gap between the two numbers didn't change when both moved the same amount, the same direction.

mastery.evidence: Correctly compensates a subtraction problem using the same-direction rule, distinct from the addition rule, for 2 examples.
